## Overview In HY V3 streaming mode, the `hy_v3` tool parser produces invalid JSON for tool-call arguments as soon as a string value contains a control character other than `\n`, `\r` or `\t`. To fix this, the partial value is now escaped with `json.dumps`, the same way `hy_v4` already does. This matters for coding agents: terminal output with ANSI colour codes (`\x1b[31m...`) is routinely passed as a tool argument (e.g. saving a build log with a `write_file` tool), and every such streamed call currently fails to parse on the client. Non-streaming is unaffected, so the bug only shows up when streaming. ## Claims - Streamed tool-call arguments are valid JSON and equal to the non-streaming arguments for any string value, including control characters. - No change for values without such characters: printable text and `\\ " \n \r \t` are escaped exactly as before. - Adds a regression test. ## Validation **Unit tests** (CPU): ```bash VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu python -m pytest -q tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v3_tool_parser.py ``` | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | new `test_partial_string_value_json_escaped` (3 cases) | 2 failed, 1 passed | 3 passed | | whole file | n/a | 17 passed | `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. **Serving path.** The real model (`tencent/Hy3-preview`, ~299B params, ~600 GB in BF16) can't run on the hardware available to me. So I validated through `OpenAIServingChat` with the real Hy3 tokenizer and a mocked engine that replays a fixed model output one token at a time, built from the helpers in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py`. Streamed vs non-streamed `arguments` for a `write_file(path, content)` call: | `content` | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | `hello world` | ✅ | ✅ | | ANSI output `\x1b[31mERROR\x1b[0m: build failed` | ❌ invalid JSON, `...build failedild failed` | ✅ | | form feed `page1\x0cpage2` | ❌ invalid JSON, `...page22` | ✅ | | backspace `abc\x08d` | ❌ invalid JSON, `...dd` | ✅ |
Serving-path script (run from the repo root with VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=.) ```python """HY V3 tool parser through vLLM's real chat-completion serving path. The real model (tencent/Hy3-preview, ~299B params) can't run here, so the engine is replaced by a fake that replays a fixed model output, tokenized with the real Hy3 tokenizer and streamed one token per RequestOutput (like AsyncLLM in DELTA mode). Everything after the engine is real vLLM code: OpenAIServingChat, the hy_v3 tool parser and SSE chunk generation, both streaming and non-streaming. For each argument value, prints whether the streamed tool-call arguments are valid JSON and equal to the non-streaming arguments. Run from the vLLM clone: VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python """ import asyncio import json from tests.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.test_serving_chat import ( MockHFConfig, _build_mock_engine, _build_renderer, _build_serving_chat, ) from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest from vllm.entrypoints.generate.base.protocol import RequestResponseMetadata from vllm.outputs import CompletionOutput, RequestOutput from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer MODEL = "tencent/Hy3-preview" TOOLS = [ { "type": "function", "function": { "name": "write_file", "parameters": { "type": "object", "properties": { "path": {"type": "string"}, "content": {"type": "string"}, }, "required": ["path", "content"], }, }, } ] VALUES = { "plain text": "hello world", "ANSI colour codes (terminal output)": "\x1b[31mERROR\x1b[0m: build failed", "form feed": "page1\x0cpage2", "backspace": "abc\x08d", } def model_output(content: str) -> str: return ( "\nwrite_file" "\npath\nout.txt" f"\ncontent\n{content}" "\n\n" ) def build(): engine = _build_mock_engine() cfg = engine.model_config cfg.model = cfg.tokenizer = MODEL cfg.hf_config = cfg.hf_text_config = MockHFConfig(model_type="hy_v3") cfg.max_model_len = 4096 engine.renderer = _build_renderer(cfg) serving = _build_serving_chat(engine, tool_parser="hy_v3", enable_auto_tools=True) return serving, get_tokenizer(MODEL) def request_output(req, text, token_ids, finished): out = CompletionOutput( index=0, text=text, token_ids=token_ids, cumulative_logprob=0.0, logprobs=None, finish_reason="stop" if finished else None, ) return RequestOutput( request_id=req.request_id, prompt=None, prompt_token_ids=[1, 2, 3], prompt_logprobs=None, outputs=[out], finished=finished, ) async def run(serving, tok, text, stream): req = ChatCompletionRequest( model=MODEL, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "save the build log"}], tools=TOOLS, stream=stream, ) ids = tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False) assert tok.decode(ids) == text, "tokenizer round-trip changed the text" async def results(): if not stream: yield request_output(req, text, ids, True) return prev = "" for i in range(1, len(ids) + 1): cur = tok.decode(ids[:i]) yield request_output(req, cur[len(prev):], [ids[i - 1]], i == len(ids)) prev = cur common = dict( request=req, result_generator=results(), request_id=req.request_id, model_name=MODEL, conversation=[], tokenizer=tok, request_metadata=RequestResponseMetadata(request_id=req.request_id), ) if not stream: parser = serving.parser_cls(tok, req.tools) resp = await serving.chat_completion_full_generator(parser=parser, **common) return [c.function.arguments for c in resp.choices[0].message.tool_calls] args = {} async for chunk in serving.chat_completion_stream_generator(**common): payload = chunk.removeprefix("data: ").strip() if not payload or payload == "[DONE]": continue for choice in json.loads(payload).get("choices", []): for tc in (choice.get("delta") or {}).get("tool_calls") or []: fn = tc.get("function") or {} args[tc["index"]] = args.get(tc["index"], "") + (fn.get("arguments") or "") return [args[i] for i in sorted(args)] async def main(): serving, tok = build() bad = 0 for label, value in VALUES.items(): text = model_output(value) ns = await run(serving, tok, text, stream=False) st = await run(serving, tok, text, stream=True) print(f"\n{label}: {value!r}") print(f" non-streaming: {ns}") print(f" streaming: {st}") try: ok = len(ns) == len(st) == 1 and json.loads(st[0]) == json.loads(ns[0]) print(f" streamed args valid JSON, equal to non-streaming: {ok}") except json.JSONDecodeError as e: ok = False print(f" streamed args INVALID JSON: {e}") bad += not ok print(f"\nmismatches: {bad}/{len(VALUES)}") asyncio.run(main()) ```
## Details **Root cause.** While a string value is still open, `HYV3ToolParser` streams a JSON prefix without the closing quote and escapes the partial value by hand, handling only `\\ " \n \r \t`. Any other control character is sent raw, which is invalid inside a JSON string. When the call closes, the rest is sliced from `json.dumps(final_args, ensure_ascii=False)` by the number of characters already streamed. `json.dumps` writes those characters as escapes (`\u001b`, `\f`), so the offsets no longer match and part of the value is sent twice. **Fix.** `escaped_val = json.dumps(partial_value, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]`. JSON escaping works per character, so the escaped prefix is always a prefix of the escaped full value. `ensure_ascii=False` matches the final `json.dumps`. This is the same line `hy_v4_tool_parser.py` already uses. **Not a duplicate.** I searched issues and PRs for `hy_v3`, `HYV3ToolParser`, `hy_v3 streaming`, `hy_v3 escape` and `tool parser control character`. Nothing covers this. #59620 edits the same file (truncated streams) but not the escaping. ---

files.patch:
@@ -272,3 +272,27 @@ def test_all_in_one_delta_streaming(self, hy_v3_tool_parser, mock_request):
         tc = _collect_streaming_tool_calls(results)
         assert len(tc) == 1 and tc[0]["name"] == "get_current_date"
         assert json.loads(tc[0]["arguments"]) == {}
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
+        "city", ["page1\x0cpage2", "red\x1b[0m\x08", 'a\\b"c\nd\re\tf']
+    )
+    def test_partial_string_value_json_escaped(
+        self, hy_v3_tool_parser, mock_request, city
+    ):
+        """A string value streamed before </arg_value> must be escaped exactly
+        as the final json.dumps escapes it, control characters included."""
+        deltas = [
+            "<tool_calls>",
+            "\n<tool_call>",
+            "get_weather",
+            "<tool_sep>",
+            "\n<arg_key>city</arg_key>",
+            f"\n<arg_value>{city[:6]}",
+            f"{city[6:]}</arg_value>",
+            "\n</tool_call>",
+            "\n</tool_calls>",
+        ]
+        results = _simulate_streaming(hy_v3_tool_parser, deltas, mock_request)
+        tc = _collect_streaming_tool_calls(results)
+        assert len(tc) == 1 and tc[0]["name"] == "get_weather"
+        assert json.loads(tc[0]["arguments"]) == {"city": city}

@@ -617,13 +617,7 @@ def _extract_streaming_incremental(
             # WITHOUT the closing quote, so the prefix stays stable
             # as the value grows.  The closing `"` and `}` will be
             # sent when the value or tool_call closes.
-            escaped_val = (
-                partial_value.replace("\\", "\\\\")
-                .replace('"', '\\"')
-                .replace("\n", "\\n")
-                .replace("\r", "\\r")
-                .replace("\t", "\\t")
-            )
+            escaped_val = json.dumps(partial_value, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
             # Note: no closing " here – it's appended only on close
             snapshot_parts.append(f'{k_json}: "{escaped_val}')
